list the things Collective Shout has caused

Collective Shout has run hundreds of campaigns, so this is the major documented list rather than every removed ad or product. “Caused” varies: some companies explicitly acted after its campaign; in other cases it was one pressure group among several.

Gaming and entertainment

Steam and itch.io 2025 adult-game crackdown. Collective Shout targeted Visa, Mastercard, PayPal and other payment processors after Valve did not respond to its campaign. Steam added a rule tying permitted content to payment-processor standards and removed hundreds of games. Itch.io temporarily deindexed essentially its entire NSFW catalogue—reportedly more than 20,000 games—while auditing it. (The Guardian)

Removal of games far beyond the specific rape/incest titles it named. Itch.io broad response swept up adult games generally, including games concerning queer identity and sexuality, rather than only titles accused of glorifying sexual abuse. (The Guardian)

Reduced payment access for adult indie games. Itch.io suspended Stripe purchases for 18+ content and began searching for payment processors willing to handle it. (GamesRadar+)

Removal of No Mercy. Its campaign helped get the game geoblocked in Australia, Canada and the UK, removed from Steam and itch.io and ultimately withdrawn globally by its developer. (Collective Shout)

Removal of Rape Day from Steam in 2019. Collective Shout participated in the international campaign against it and claimed the removal as a victory. (Collective Shout)

Grand Theft Auto V pulled from Target and Kmart stores in Australia in 2014. This was not a nationwide legal ban; the two retailers stopped stocking it following the campaign. (ABC News)

A Serbian Film effectively banned from Australian commercial exhibition and sale. Collective Shout sought review of its R18+ classification, after which the Classification Review Board changed it to “Refused Classification.” (Collective Shout)

Tyler, the Creator’s 2015 Australian tour was cancelled amid its visa campaign. He was not formally banned at that point—his application remained undecided—but the tour was abandoned because of the surrounding controversy. (The Guardian)

Retail products, platforms and publications

Coles stopped stocking Zoo Weekly. Collective Shout supported the campaign that preceded Coles’ decision. The magazine closed shortly afterward, but its publisher blamed “tough retail conditions,” so saying Collective Shout single-handedly killed the magazine would be unsupported. (9News)

7-Eleven and BP removed People and Picture magazines, and publisher Bauer later stopped publishing those titles, following a Collective Shout campaign. (Collective Shout)

Childlike sex dolls and related listings were removed from numerous marketplaces, including Wish, Alibaba, Shopee, Etsy and Temu, following reports or campaigns by the group. Temu later removed all sex dolls; Shein also removed them, although France’s threat to block Shein was another major cause. (Collective Shout)

Seller and promoter accounts were terminated across X, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube. Examples include 71 X accounts, nine Instagram accounts in 2023, additional large accounts in 2025, and a US seller’s website being seized after reports. (Collective Shout)

Sexualised children’s merchandise was withdrawn, including hundreds of TeePublic baby onesies, Shein baby fishnets, toddler clothing and toys, and other products. (Collective Shout)

Other products were removed, including Spotlight “pimp” costumes, offensive trucker caps, penis-shaped pacifiers, Pornhub shirts and various Playboy products. (Collective Shout)

Andrew Tate courses were removed from Spotify and SoundCloud after a Collective Shout petition received approximately 155,000 signatures. (Collective Shout)

Advertising, events and corporate activity

Numerous advertisements and displays were removed or altered, including an H&M school-uniform ad, Honey Birdette shopfront ads, an AirAsia “Get off in Thailand” campaign, an AI-generated Shein ad, UltraTune’s long-running ads and various billboards and social-media promotions. (Collective Shout)

Wicked Camper vans became subject to deregistration mechanisms when owners refused to remove slogans found in breach of advertising standards. The broader campaign also persuaded Lonely Planet to withdraw its endorsement and a festival to exclude the vans. (Collective Shout)

The international beach-handball bikini requirement was abolished after the broader #LetThemWearShorts campaign in which Collective Shout participated. (Collective Shout)

Events and commercial collaborations were cancelled. Claimed examples include an Atlanta Hawks/strip-club collaboration, Playboy-themed events, porn-performer Schoolies arrangements and associated hotel bookings or billboards. These generally involved several complainants or organisations, so Collective Shout was not necessarily the sole cause. (Collective Shout)

Some investors divested shares connected with Playboy or strip-club operator RCI Hospitality. Collective Shout contacted investment firms and claims multiple firms subsequently sold their holdings. (Collective Shout)

Laws and platform regulation it helped push

Australia’s pornography age-verification trial. Collective Shout campaigned for the government to reverse its earlier rejection of a trial and later served on its stakeholder advisory board. It was one contributor, not the sole cause. (Collective Shout)

Stricter Australian online-age rules, including advocacy for the social-media minimum age of 16 and inclusion of services such as Snapchat and YouTube. Again, this was part of a much larger political process. (Collective Shout)

Deepfake sexual-abuse offences in several Australian states. The group has lobbied on the issue since 2019 and claims partial credit for legislation or proposed legislation in New South Wales, South Australia and Queensland. (Collective Shout)

Chub.ai was geoblocked in Australia after Collective Shout reported content to the eSafety regulator. (Collective Shout)

Major unintended consequences

A system of financial censorship extending beyond illegal material. Its payment-processor strategy demonstrated that card networks can determine what legal fictional works may be sold worldwide without legislation or a court order. (The Guardian)

Loss of visibility and likely revenue for thousands of unrelated indie developers, including adult, artistic and LGBTQ-themed creators who were not accused of producing rape or child-abuse games. (The Guardian)

A huge counter-campaign against Visa, Mastercard and PayPal, including a petition exceeding 150,000 signatures and organised calls to payment companies. (The Guardian)

Severe harassment of Collective Shout personnel. Following the game-removal campaign, staff received rape and death threats, doxxing attempts and sexualised AI deepfakes. The perpetrators—not Collective Shout—are responsible for those attacks, but the attacks were a direct backlash to the campaign. (News.com.au

Things it attempted but did not cause include banning Snoop Dogg and Eminem from Australia and banning Detroit: Become Human. Snoop Dogg received his visa despite its petition; Tyler’s tour cancellation should likewise not be misreported as an official Australian ban. (The Guardian)

@CyberTechWolff @grok 这是 GPT 说 Collective Shout 造成的。所以其中很多事情都出现了权力真空。如果我在我的游戏网络里这么做，哪些事情最不费力就能走红？

列出 Collective Shout 造成的事情

Collective Shout 发起过数百场运动，所以这是主要的有记录清单，而不是每一个被移除的广告或产品。“造成”这个说法因情况而异：有些公司明确是在其运动之后采取行动；另一些情况下，它只是多个施压团体之一。

游戏和娱乐

Steam 和 itch.io 2025 年成人游戏整顿。Collective Shout 在 Valve 没有回应其运动后，将目标对准了 Visa、Mastercard、PayPal 和其他支付处理商。Steam 增加了一条规则，将允许的内容与支付处理商标准挂钩，并移除了数百款游戏。Itch.io 在审核期间暂时基本取消索引了其整个 NSFW 目录——据称超过 20,000 款游戏。（The Guardian）

移除的游戏远远超出其点名的具体强奸/乱伦题材作品。Itch.io 的广泛回应总体上波及成人游戏，包括涉及酷儿身份和性取向的游戏，而不只是被指控美化性虐待的作品。（The Guardian）

成人独立游戏的支付渠道减少。Itch.io 暂停了 18+ 内容的 Stripe 购买，并开始寻找愿意处理此类内容的支付处理商。（GamesRadar+）

《No Mercy》被移除。其运动帮助使该游戏在澳大利亚、加拿大和英国被地理封锁，从 Steam 和 itch.io 下架，并最终由其开发者在全球范围内撤回。（Collective Shout）

《Rape Day》于 2019 年从 Steam 移除。Collective Shout 参与了反对它的国际运动，并将其移除称为一场胜利。（Collective Shout）

《Grand Theft Auto V》于 2014 年从澳大利亚 Target 和 Kmart 门店下架。这并不是全国性的法律禁令；这两家零售商是在该运动之后停止进货。（ABC News）

《A Serbian Film》实际上被禁止在澳大利亚进行商业放映和销售。Collective Shout 要求复审其 R18+ 分级，之后 Classification Review Board 将其改为“Refused Classification”。（Collective Shout）

Tyler, the Creator 的 2015 年澳大利亚巡演在其签证运动期间被取消。当时他并未被正式禁止入境——他的申请仍未决定——但由于周围争议，巡演被放弃。（The Guardian）

零售产品、平台和出版物

Coles 停止销售 Zoo Weekly。Collective Shout 支持了 Coles 做出决定之前的那场运动。该杂志不久后停刊，但其出版商将原因归咎于“艰难的零售环境”，所以说 Collective Shout 单独扼杀了这本杂志是缺乏依据的。（9News）

在 Collective Shout 发起运动后，7-Eleven 和 BP 下架了 People 和 Picture 杂志，出版商 Bauer 后来也停止出版这些刊物。（Collective Shout）

在该团体的举报或运动之后，包括 Wish、Alibaba、Shopee、Etsy 和 Temu 在内的众多市场下架了儿童化性玩偶及相关商品列表。Temu 后来移除了所有性玩偶；Shein 也移除了它们，不过法国威胁封锁 Shein 是另一个主要原因。（Collective Shout）

卖家和推广者账号在 X、Instagram、TikTok 和 YouTube 上被终止。例如包括 71 个 X 账号、2023 年的 9 个 Instagram 账号、2025 年其他大型账号，以及一家美国卖家的网站在被举报后遭查封。（Collective Shout）

带有儿童性化内容的商品被下架，包括数百件 TeePublic 婴儿连体衣、Shein 婴儿网袜、幼儿服装和玩具，以及其他产品。（Collective Shout）

其他产品也被移除，包括 Spotlight 的“皮条客”服装、冒犯性的卡车司机帽、阴茎形状的安抚奶嘴、Pornhub 衬衫以及各种 Playboy 产品。（Collective Shout）

在 Collective Shout 的请愿获得约 155,000 个签名后，Andrew Tate 的课程被 Spotify 和 SoundCloud 下架。（Collective Shout）

广告、活动和企业行为

大量广告和展示被移除或修改，包括 H&M 校服广告、Honey Birdette 店面广告、AirAsia 的“Get off in Thailand”（在泰国下机/爽一下）活动、一则 AI 生成的 Shein 广告、UltraTune 长期投放的广告，以及各种广告牌和社交媒体推广。（Collective Shout）

当 Wicked Camper 露营车的车主拒绝移除被认定违反广告标准的标语时，这些车辆开始受到注销登记机制的约束。更广泛的活动还说服 Lonely Planet 撤回其背书，并让一个节庆活动将这些露营车排除在外。（Collective Shout）

在 Collective Shout 参与的更广泛的 #LetThemWearShorts 活动之后，国际沙滩手球比赛要求穿比基尼的规定被废除。（Collective Shout）

一些活动和商业合作被取消。声称的例子包括 Atlanta Hawks/脱衣舞俱乐部合作、Playboy 主题活动、色情表演者参与的 Schoolies 毕业狂欢安排，以及相关酒店预订或广告牌。这些通常涉及多名投诉者或多个组织，因此 Collective Shout 不一定是唯一原因。（Collective Shout）

一些投资者撤出了与 Playboy 或脱衣舞俱乐部运营商 RCI Hospitality 相关的股票。Collective Shout 联系了投资公司，并声称多家公司随后出售了其持股。（Collective Shout）

它帮助推动的法律和平台监管

澳大利亚的色情内容年龄验证试点。Collective Shout 曾发起活动，要求政府推翻此前拒绝试点的决定，后来还加入了该试点的利益相关方咨询委员会。它是推动因素之一，而不是唯一原因。（Collective Shout）

更严格的澳大利亚在线年龄规则，包括倡导将社交媒体最低年龄设为 16 岁，并纳入 Snapchat 和 YouTube 等服务。同样，这是一个更大政治过程的一部分。（Collective Shout）

澳大利亚多个州的深度伪造性虐待犯罪。该组织自 2019 年以来一直就这一问题进行游说，并声称对新南威尔士州、南澳大利亚州和昆士兰州的立法或拟议立法有部分功劳。（Collective Shout）

在 Collective Shout 向 eSafety 监管机构举报内容后，Chub.ai 在澳大利亚被地理封锁。（Collective Shout）

重大的意外后果

一种超出非法材料范围的金融审查制度。其支付处理商策略表明，银行卡网络可以在没有立法或法院命令的情况下，决定哪些合法的虚构作品可以在全球销售。（The Guardian）

数千名无关的独立开发者失去了曝光度，并很可能损失收入，其中包括成人、艺术和 LGBTQ 主题创作者；他们并未被指控制作强奸或儿童虐待游戏。（The Guardian）

针对 Visa、Mastercard 和 PayPal 的大规模反制活动，包括一份签名超过 150,000 的请愿书，以及有组织地致电支付公司。（The Guardian）

对 Collective Shout 人员的严重骚扰。在游戏下架运动之后，工作人员收到了强奸和死亡威胁、被人试图人肉搜索，以及被制作带有性意味的 AI 深度伪造内容。应对这些攻击负责的是施害者——不是 Collective Shout——但这些攻击是对该运动的直接反弹。（News.com.au

它曾试图推动但并未造成的事情包括禁止 Snoop Dogg 和 Eminem 进入澳大利亚，以及禁售 Detroit: Become Human。尽管有请愿，Snoop Dogg 仍然拿到了签证；Tyler 的巡演取消同样不应被误报为澳大利亚官方禁令。（The Guardian）

"The 'Liang Cycle' Has Been Broken"

**Concept of the "Liang Cycle":** High-Flyer Quant (with AUM exceeding RMB 70 billion, average return of 56.55% in 2025) generated profits to fund DeepSeek, while DeepSeek in turn fed back into the quant business, creating a perpetual‑motion machine. In July 2026, all nine of High-Flyer's showcase products recorded monthly drawdowns exceeding 20% (with the largest at -22.15%), and eight had turned negative year‑to‑date. Other top quant firms such as Mingshi, Jiukun, and Minghong also experienced synchronous drawdowns, hence the cycle was broken. Verification: High-Flyer's AUM over RMB 70 billion and its 2025 average return of 56.55% come from PaiPaiWang, republished via Caijing, Modern Express, and Sina. As of the July 31, 2026 cut‑off, High-Flyer's nine showcase products had eight with negative year‑to‑date performance and all down over 20% for the month, consistent with the original text. "“梁循环”已被打破"

**“梁循环”的概念：** 幻方量化（AUM 超过人民币 700 亿元，2025 年平均收益率为 56.55%）产生利润来资助 DeepSeek，而 DeepSeek 又反哺量化业务，形成一台永动机。2026 年 7 月，幻方所有九只展示产品的月度回撤均超过 20%（最大为 -22.15%），其中八只年内收益已转负。其他头部量化机构，如明汯、九坤和鸣石，也出现同步回撤，因此这一循环被打破。核实：幻方 AUM 超过人民币 700 亿元以及其 2025 年平均收益率 56.55% 来自排排网，并经《财经》、现代快报和新浪转载。截至 2026 年 7 月 31 日截点，幻方九只展示产品中有八只年内业绩为负，且全部当月下跌超过 20%，与原文一致。明汯、九坤和鸣石 7 月在 10%–30% 区间的回撤，有第一财经、中金在线和好买的数据支持，但“集体崩盘”这一说法是主观概括，而非统一基准结论。DeepSeek 首轮外部融资约人民币 510 亿元（2026 年 6 月完成），梁文锋个人出资约人民币 200 亿元，腾讯出资人民币 100 亿元，CATL 出资人民币 50 亿元等，已有媒体报道，但未获相关公司确认。原文称“幻方年利润约为人民币 50 亿元”以及“一轮融资等于幻方十年利润”，这是算术估算（基于人民币 700 亿元 AUM × 约 7% 净收益假设），并非经审计数据，标记为**无法核实**。“全球 AI 首富梁文锋”的说法没有权威富豪榜依据，标记为**无法核实**。

“DeepSeek 不再依赖幻方”这一核心判断在时间顺序上是成立的：DeepSeek 于 2023 年 7 月从幻方 AI 团队中拆分出来；前三年，其研发算力由幻方分红资助；在 2026 年 6 月人民币 510 亿元首轮外部融资完成后，其资本结构转向由外部股权主导。梁个人出资人民币 200 亿元源自其累积的幻方收益，但如今已进入其个人资产端，而不是由幻方实体输送。然而，“柴火已经烧尽，引擎已经启动”这一说法混淆了法律边界——幻方量化（宁波幻方 + 浙江九章）和杭州 DeepSeek 是两个独立持牌/注册实体。量化回撤不会直接触发 DeepSeek 现金流断裂，但可能影响梁个人后续跟投能力，以及幻方作为 LP 继续出资的潜在意愿。幻方 2025 年的高收益来自退出中性策略并转向纯多头，押注 TMT 动量；2026 年 7 月的回撤源自同一因素的反转（科创 50/中证 1000 急跌以及动量因子反转）——这是策略风格暴露问题，而非治理失败。

“一些博主在阴阳怪气”的情绪基调，本质上反映的是对法律独立性与个人关联的简单混同。可验证的事实链条是：High-Flyer Quant 在 2025 年的高收益（56.55%）→ 2026 年 7 月全行业多头指数增强策略回撤（High-Flyer 单月 -20%+，行业多头平均 -16.94%）→ DeepSeek 于 2026 年 6 月完成 510 亿元人民币首轮融资，估值为 3250 亿–3571 亿元人民币 → 量化业绩波动不再构成 DeepSeek 生存的必要条件。不可验证的链条包括：将 “Liang Cycle” 量化建模为一台金融永动机、High-Flyer 对 DeepSeek 的隐性连带责任，以及 Liang 的个人财富排名。从保守视角看，量化回撤会损害 Liang 的个人信用和后续投资能力。从中性视角看，两个实体已经脱钩；量化净值与 AI 研发无关。从激进视角看，510 亿元人民币融资本身就是对 High-Flyer 时代结束的宣告；真正的变量在于第二轮估值能否维持在 3500 亿元人民币以上。
